authored_by: coordinator, to the specification in FREEZE ADDENDUM 3 and the coordinator's explicit split
note: The prior challenge adjudication returned confirm_B / surface-only / not-MIXED, and its reason was precisely that the rubric never separates controlled from uncontrolled breaks. Addendum 3 makes that separation constructive rather than a caveat: the candidate-real component below is the criterion the adjudicator said would be needed before 'deliberate stylistic control' could be named as a parent.

components.name: One-line beats that earn their isolation
components.instruction: This story may set short lines or single sentences off on their own. Judge whether those isolations do dramatic work IN CONTEXT: an isolated line should land a turn, a reveal, a shift of attention, or a beat of silence that the surrounding prose has set up, and the story should return to ordinary paragraphing when nothing is being marked. Score 1.0 when nearly every isolated line is placed where a beat belongs and the effect would be lost if it were folded back into the preceding paragraph. Score 0.5 when some isolations do work and others are arbitrary. Score 0.0 when lines are isolated indiscriminately or habitually, so the breaks mark nothing in particular, AND also 0.0 when the story isolates nothing but plainly needed a beat somewhere. Answer NA only if the story is too short to show any paragraphing pattern. Judge the placement, not the quantity: a story with three well-placed breaks scores higher than one with thirty indiscriminate ones.
components.rationale: Isolates the candidate-REAL component: deliberate one-line beats serving tension and pacing, judged in context. Explicitly decouples from density (three well-placed breaks beat thirty indiscriminate ones) so it can score high where the surface component scores low and vice versa.

components.name: Blank-line and short-paragraph density
components.instruction: Count the typographic density of the story's paragraphing: what fraction of its paragraphs are a single short clause or sentence set off by its own line break, and how much blank vertical space the text uses overall. Score 1.0 when most paragraphs are one-line beats and the text is visually very airy; 0.5 when there is a moderate mix; 0.0 when the story is built from ordinary multi-sentence paragraphs with little blank space. Count the formatting only. Pay no attention to whether any break is well placed, whether it marks anything, or whether the story reads better or worse for it.
components.rationale: Isolates the SURFACE component: the blank-line / paste-formatting habit alone, counted with no judgement of effect. This is the component the two retired parent channels were actually measuring.
